main_text.p: vectigal cerevisiæ & vino in tabernis aut diversoriis publicis imponere, & singulis femestrib. locare tanti, quanti id proximè fecerant oppidani, pecuniamq; illam stipendiis impendere, ac salariis officiariorum suorum, & negotiis aliis necessariis: quod si tamen vectigal annum excesserit aureos quatermille, excedens pars ut cedat in ærarium commune, ejusq; quæstori numeretur.

p.i: In hoc statu res hæsit[?], cum hæc recognoscerem. Sequitur de aliis ad civitatis dignitatem & jura pertinentibus.

main_text.head: ALIA PRÆCLARA CIVITATIS IVRA ET LEGES.
main_text.p: Habet vero præter hæc alia quoq; præclara jura civitas hæc nostra. Inter quæ illud censeri potest, quod in toto Præclara iu-ra ac privile-gia civitatis. ANGLIAE regno commerciorum ac negociationum libertatem jam ccc, xlv ante annos cives habuerint cum conditionib. haud pœnitendis: ut testatur diploma Henrici iii regis anno regni eius XLI signatum, quod est in reip. archivis illæsum. Deinde illud etiam, quod ante complures hominum ætates amplissimo FOEDERI ANSEATICO civitas adscripta sit, locumq; in eo perhonestū inter civitates socias tenuerit[?] semper, & ad-

page.notes: The large woodcut initial at the start of the paragraph reads as H (joined to "abet"); reconstructed as "Habet" and not certain of the initial. "hæsit" in the italic line is doubtful: the letter looks like f, copied as the likely reading. "tenuerit" is doubtful. "Graninga" in the second left note is unclear; the printed name may be Groninga. The left-margin note reads "Graninga socia fœde-ris Anseatici" in the scan; the first word is doubtful. "adscripta" is read from a form resembling "affcripta", with long s. "perhonestū" carries a tilde over u. No catchword: the page ends mid-word on "ad-", which continues onto the next page. Note 2 ("Groninga socia fœde-ris Anseatici.") is not transcribed as its own element because its position beside the text could not be confirmed with certainty; its text is given in the notes.
